claims.statement: Management guide covers FPT/GHEC and requires repository admin to configure custom domains; publishing-source maintainer permission must not be generalized to custom-domain administration.

Recommended ordering is verify ownership first, add custom domain to Pages repository settings, then configure provider DNS. DNS configured before repository association can expose subdomain takeover risk; no native changes are authorized by the source.
DNS propagation can take up to 24 hours. Windows alternatives to dig are Resolve-DnsName or installing BIND; instructions are examples, not executed dependencies or current tool recommendations.

Apex requires repository custom-domain setting and ALIAS, ANAME or A records; IPv6 AAAA is optional in the earlier procedure, with A strongly recommended alongside AAAA. Later summary says add all A and AAAA or only ALIAS/ANAME; preserve the IPv6 obligation discrepancy rather than silently impose one interpretation.

Saving domain for branch publishing creates a CNAME commit at source-branch root. Custom Actions publishing creates no CNAME file, ignores existing CNAME and does not require it; repository CNAME file is not a DNS-provider CNAME record.
ALIAS/ANAME apex target is the default site domain. Pinned A and AAAA endpoint lists are historical source evidence, not freshly verified DNS addresses or permission to replace live records.

Source advises removing a provider-created default record before proceeding. Any actual removal requires exact record identity and dependency/blast-radius review; documentation does not authorize indiscriminate DNS deletion.

Wildcard DNS is strongly discouraged even for verified domains: verification can protect an immediate subdomain while a deeper descendant remains takeover-exposed. Verification must not be generalized to recursive wildcard protection.
dig examples check record answers against expected targets, not repository ownership verification, successful TLS issuance, effective site privacy or observed HTTP behavior.

Locally generated branch output should incorporate the settings-created CNAME commit before pushing generated files. This synchronization requirement does not apply as an effective-domain mechanism to custom Actions sources that ignore CNAME.
Enforce HTTPS is an optional setting and may take up to 24 hours to become available; checkbox selection or availability alone does not prove valid certificate, redirects or absence of mixed content.

Apex/www paired redirect requires correct provider records for both names. www CNAME must point directly to user.github.io or organization.github.io without repository name; a redirect expectation is not a runtime receipt.
Subdomain setup adds repository domain first and then provider CNAME. Internationalized domains must be entered Punycode-encoded in the documented settings flow.

Public and private Pages use the same user/organization default-domain CNAME targets; do not point provider CNAME at the unique *.pages.github.io settings hostname. Private publication availability is GHEC-specific and DNS target alone does not confer reader authorization.

Pointing custom subdomain to apex rather than the default Pages domain can cause HTTPS enforcement and reachability problems. This warning is separate from legitimate paired-name redirects configured through the default target.

DNS summary separates @ apex A/AAAA or ALIAS/ANAME records from subdomain CNAME. Documentation examples contain placeholder domains and illustrative response addresses, not records to apply to this estate.

Removing a domain through repository Pages settings may resolve another-repository association conflict; changing that other repository requires separate authority and can affect inherited project URLs. Remove setting does not itself prove provider DNS cleanup or safe recovery.

Disabled site with lingering unverified domain DNS remains takeover-exposed; source recommends prompt update/removal. All extracted procedures remain reference-only, with no DNS, certificate, domain, protection or publication action performed.
